chunks: Whosoever desires honour (should remember) that all honour is with God. All good words ascend to Him, and all good deeds He exalts. As for those who are plotting evil, there is severe punishment for them, and their plots will be fruitless.

key_terms.الْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ: Righteous deed, which is exalted by God
key_terms.الْعِزَّةُ: Honour or dignity, specifically belonging to God
key_terms.الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ: Good word or speech, which ascends to God

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'al-izzah' (honour) in Surah Al-Fatiir and how do good deeds ascend to God?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to establish the principle of 'al-Kalimah al-Tayyibah' (the pure word), where the 'word' is interpreted as the declaration of God's oneness and the Prophet's prophethood, which ascends alongside righteous deeds. It highlights the divine reciprocity where human effort is elevated by God, contrasting the transient nature of human plotting (makr) with the enduring honor (izzah) that belongs solely to the Originator.
